summary: @servicetitan/hammer-icon preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute a 727KB obfuscated bundle
details: The npm package @servicetitan/hammer-icon@1.2.6 advertises itself as a Material Design SVG icon set but ships two files that are not declared in package.json's `files` whitelist: `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js`. package.json registers `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`, so `setup.mjs` runs automatically on `npm install`. `setup.mjs` checks whether `bun` is available on PATH; if not, it downloads a pinned Bun runtime (v1.3.13) from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v${V}/${platform}.zip`, extracts it to a tmpdir, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync` to run the sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB bundle prefixed with `// @bun @bun-cjs` and protected by string-array rotation obfuscation (function `WV8StW` rotating array `n7gIxM`), with no relationship to SVG icon rendering. An icon package has no legitimate reason to pull a second language runtime at install time in order to execute an obfuscated bundle that its own `files` manifest does not acknowledge. The scope name `@servicetitan/*` matches a real organization but the tarball contents are inconsistent with a first-party icon publish, indicating typosquat impersonation or scope compromise. Installing this package auto-executes attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine via a runtime fetched at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
